---
title: "NestedTurbulence"
subtitle: "Adaptively subcycled nested-grid MHD with constrained transport or GLM cleaning"
toc: false
---

This report describes **NestedMHD**, a nested-grid ideal-MHD solver written in Julia on
[KernelAbstractions](https://github.com/JuliaGPU/KernelAbstractions.jl), so one source runs on
CPUs and on CUDA, Metal and ROCm GPUs. It joins two lines of earlier work:

- the **GLMMHDTurb** solver ([yipihey/GLMMHDTurb](https://github.com/yipihey/GLMMHDTurb)): PLM
  with the MonCen limiter, a three-dimensional MUSCL-Hancock predictor, HLL/HLLD Riemann
  solvers and Dedner GLM cleaning, tuned for GPU throughput;
- its **constrained-transport fix** ([Solaceonx/GLMMHDTurb, branch `sweep-fixes`](https://github.com/Solaceonx/GLMMHDTurb/tree/sweep-fixes)):
  face-staggered magnetic field with Gardiner–Stone (2005) upwinded edge EMFs, which keeps
  $\nabla\cdot\mathbf B$ at rounding;
- the **subcycled cascade driver** of the Rust `cascade_gravity` code, whose design (Berger–Colella
  refluxing, Balsara-type EMF restriction across levels) is carried over and extended.

Each hierarchy uses one of two $\nabla\cdot\mathbf B$ treatments, constrained transport or GLM.
It is nested in static ratio-2 patches and advanced with **adaptive per-level time steps**:
every level takes its own CFL step, so coarse levels take far fewer steps than their children. The
coarse–fine boundary is filled with **second-order time-interpolated ghost zones**.

## Results at a glance

| Claim | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Mass, momentum and energy are conserved to rounding across 2- and 3-level nests | @sec-conservation |
| CT keeps $\lvert\nabla\cdot\mathbf B\rvert\,\Delta x/\max\lvert\mathbf B\rvert \sim 10^{-15}$ on every level, from $t=0$ on | @sec-conservation, @sec-ot-run |
| Time-interpolated ghost zones converge at 2nd order (1.98–2.00); stale ghosts at 1st (0.86–0.95); at $N=128$ stale ghosts double the child's error | @sec-ghost |
| The port reproduces GLMMHDTurb's Orszag–Tang $v_\mathrm{rms}$ to four digits (0.7887 / 0.7906) | @sec-otref |
| Per-level adaptive steps do 2.8× fewer cell updates than fixed ratio-2 subcycling on a cold dense core | @sec-adaptive |
| In 2-D Mach-10 driven turbulence, the time mean of $\ln\rho$ at one point agrees with the volume mean within 1.4 error bars in all 8 runs; the variance of one run does not converge to the ensemble value in 10 crossing times | @sec-ergo-ensemble |

Everything here was run on a CPU (two threads). The kernels are backend-generic KernelAbstractions
code, but **no GPU backend has been compiled or run for this report**. @sec-roadmap says what that
means for performance.
